query: For high-entropy-alloy materials intended for self-lubricating moving components, what single intervention could reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate across a wide service-temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites prior evidence supporting it, and proposes an experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation or formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer in high-entropy alloy materials can reduce both the coefficient of friction and wear rate across a wide service-temperature range.
generation.intervention: nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation or formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer
generation.conditions: moving components, wide service-temperature range (from -20°C to 200°C)
generation.mechanism: The nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation or formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer can improve the tribological behavior of high-entropy alloy materials by reducing the contact area between the surfaces, increasing the surface hardness, and promoting the formation of a self-lubricating tribofilm.
generation.predicted_outcome: a reduction of at least 30% in the coefficient of friction and 25% in the wear rate compared to the untreated alloy
generation.uncertainty: The actual reduction in coefficient of friction and wear rate may vary depending on the specific high-entropy alloy composition, the surface roughness, and the contact pressure.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the treated high-entropy alloy material shows a reduction of less than 20% in the coefficient of friction or less than 15% in the wear rate compared to the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

goal.property: reduced coefficient of friction and wear rate

limitation.issue: high coefficient of friction and wear rate across a wide service-temperature range

prior_attempts: prior surface treatments or coatings may not be effective across a wide temperature range
